key_insight: dR-Eig-PIELM removes represented gradient modes before the Maxwell eigensolve, preventing a source of nonphysical modes that PEC boundary conditions alone cannot eliminate.
engineering_relevance: The method supports waveguide spectral analysis and geometry design using computed cutoff frequencies and their sensitivities.
method: Build compatible tensor-product grad–curl trial spaces.
Constrain the sampled PEC space to the mass-orthogonal complement of represented gradients.
Assemble symmetric weak-form Gram matrices for a one-shot multimode, symmetric-definite eigensolve.
evidence_signal: Rectangle and cuboid tests show exclusion of gradient-contaminated spurious modes, rapid polynomial-degree convergence, and competitive work–precision performance; a mapped waveguide example demonstrates a constrained local geometry update.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on sampling and material-positivity assumptions, and fixed-degree exactness is established for rectangles and cuboids rather than general geometries.
paper_title: Embedding a de Rham Complex Structure into Eig-PIELM for Maxwell Eigenvalue Problems
